Check workbook compatibility ↗
JAVASCRIPT SDK / BROWSER
import { Evaltra } from "@evaltra/engine";

const engine = Evaltra.browser();

try {
  const book = await engine.open(workbookBytes);
  await book.range("Inputs!B2")
    .setCellContents([[59]]);
  const result = await book
    .range("Summary!B8").read();
  console.log(result);
} finally {
  await engine.close();
}
Example for a workbook with Inputs and Summary sheets. Uses the locally built SDK package.




GOOD TO KNOW
A few practical
 details.
Where does Evaltra fit in an agent or ETL workflow?+
Your application maps a tool call or prepared dataset to model inputs, requests calculation and reads typed results and diagnostics. You control model access, orchestration and downstream actions.
A notebook, Databricks job or AWS Lambda function can be a client of the HTTP service where its runtime and network allow it. These are integration patterns; ready-made platform connectors and a native Python library are planned.
How do I run it on a server?+
The native Rust executable exposes workbook sessions and isolated calculations through HTTP. The server does not require Node.js or Python at runtime. Keep the service token in your application backend; sessions and job results belong to one server process.
EVALTRA_SERVICE_TOKEN=… ./evaltra-server

POST /v1/sessions
POST /v1/sessions/{id}/commands
GET  /v1/jobs/{id}
Can I use my existing Excel workbook?+
Evaltra opens XLSX workbooks and runs supported formulas with the same Rust core in native and browser environments. Validate your model's formulas and workbook features before production use.
VBA and UDF execution, Power Query, automatic external-link refresh and iterative circular calculation are outside the runtime scope. Numeric and XLSX preservation compatibility has open work; successful import is not a guarantee that every formula or feature is supported.
How do these demos work?+
This website is a static preview. Revenue and sales examples use simple browser calculations on synthetic data. The formula section implements four presets, and the comparison table displays prepared example outputs alongside recorded reference results.
No Evaltra API or engine runs on this page. The integration examples describe how you can use the product in your own application.
